title: Materiality: 96 of 101 orders are material under the illustrative project aggregation
description: With the illustrative test thresholds (single order 25,000,000 cents; 30-day window; project as the only grouping key) the materiality engine marks 96 of the 101 Builder Zero purchase orders material. That is a calibration issue with an illustrative key and window, not a default and not a finding about the engine.
linked_items: DEC-A1-8 (aggregation key and window); DEC-A1-1; golden materiality_summary
how_it_is_handled_here: Kept in the programme record. No threshold, key or window is chosen by the builder; the golden file records the observation, and later milestones use the policy as configuration.

title: Audit chain: a careful rewrite of the newest events cannot be detected by the chain alone
description: A hash chain detects edits that break a link. An attacker who recomputes the hashes of the last events leaves a chain that verifies. Detecting that needs an independent anchor of the chain head.
how_it_is_handled_here: Stated limit in the M2 contract suite; entry EDR-21 carries the full description. No change in M3.

title: Tenant isolation alone does not stop an authorised tenant user writing directly to a policy or decision record
description: The control functions check roles, but a session that holds only a tenant role could call the store directly and write a protected record kind. The port contract scopes by tenant and does not know roles.
how_it_is_handled_here: Stated limit in M2. M3 adds new kinds (recon_state, quarantine, entity_alias, entity_resolution, extracted_document, job) that need the same protection; they are named here for the Engine to decide under EDR-20, whose text is unchanged from M2.

title: The full M2 wrapper run was too slow for the auditor in one sitting
description: The auditor re-ran each M2 check separately but not the single wrapper that runs them all, which exceeded the auditor time limit.
how_it_is_handled_here: The M3 wrapper prints the time taken by each step and every step can be run on its own (RUN_COMMANDS.txt). The long mutation runs are separate commands, not part of the wrapper.
status: Handled in the package; for the auditor to confirm

title: The source name on a delivery is trusted
description: ingest_file receives a source name (for example accounting) and uses it to decide which authority rule applies. Nothing in this build checks that the person or connector delivering the file is registered for that source.
how_it_is_handled_here: Stated in the handoff register. Tests show the pipeline refuses tenant spoofing; they cannot show source spoofing is refused because that needs the Engine.

title: A job worker needs its own service identity to record a terminal failure
description: If the credentials that submitted a job are revoked or expire during retries, the tenant store refuses the dead-letter record. The reference runner keeps the failure in an unrecorded list and reports recorded false, so it is not lost silently, but a real worker needs an identity of its own to write it.
how_it_is_handled_here: Contract case JR-08 requires the failure to be reported; the identity question is in the EDR-04 decisions for Amir.

title: A whole file is written as one all-or-nothing batch
description: The pipeline writes a file as one atomic batch so a failed file leaves nothing behind. A real database may limit batch size or duration; splitting a file removes the all-or-nothing guarantee unless the receipt design is changed.
how_it_is_handled_here: This build limits a file to 100,000 rows and 5 MB by default (configuration, not a product decision).

title: The document extractor is a stand-in
description: The text reader handles the two Builder Zero quote documents. It exists to test the human-verification rule and the ambiguity handling. It is not an extraction product and was not run on any real PDF, scan or email.
how_it_is_handled_here: Extracted values are never authoritative until a person with the document_verifier role verifies them against the document hash.

title: Invoice-versus-order amount and price variance is not an ingestion check
description: Ingestion checks that an order exists and is consistent with the invoice link (PO_NOT_VISIBLE and the PO mismatch codes). Whether an invoice exceeds its order or a rate drifts is detection, and is left to M5 with thresholds from the product owner.
how_it_is_handled_here: No variance threshold exists in M3.

title: Identical purchase orders are held for a person before detection can use them (PS-17)
description: PO-0100 and PO-0101 are identical. Ingestion holds both as DUPLICATE_CANDIDATE and does not choose one. The M5 rule for surplus ordering will therefore see both as pending until a reviewer decides.
how_it_is_handled_here: Recorded so M5 handles pending orders explicitly rather than assuming both count.

title: Which missing optional values are tolerable is configuration, and the demonstration set is the builder choice
description: The default policy blocks use of any record with a missing optional value. Builder Zero needs a short tolerated list (for example GST amount on an invoice) so that most records are usable. That list is a demonstration choice, not a product decision.
how_it_is_handled_here: The list lives in demo_setup.DEMO_POLICY; a real list comes from the product owner and pilot builders. Material fields can never be tolerated.

title: A stored job result loses tenant-like keys
description: The tenant-scope guard removes tenant-like keys from anything written to the store, including a job result. The runner now returns the stored form, so a replay returns exactly what the first run returned.
how_it_is_handled_here: Behaviour is tested. Handlers should not return tenant-like keys.

title: Reissue detection is a naming pattern only
description: INV-0185 is shown as a reissue candidate of INV-0184 because of the invoice-number pattern and the credit link. That is lineage information only. It never changes a total; a person must decide.
how_it_is_handled_here: Stated in the lineage record itself.
